name: Bryan Johnson's Altos Labs
what: Advanced biotechnologies for longevity research.
how: Focusing on extending human healthspan through cutting-edge research.

name: GLP-1 Metabolic Medicines
what: Incretin-based drugs that regulate appetite and blood sugar, producing substantial weight loss and cardiovascular benefit across large trials.
how: Engineered peptides mimic gut hormones to slow gastric emptying and signal satiety, delivered as weekly injections and, increasingly, oral forms.

name: Long-Acting HIV Prevention
what: Injectable prevention given every few weeks or months instead of a daily pill, removing the adherence problem that limits oral PrEP.
how: Long-acting injectable antiretrovirals with extended-release formulation.

name: Malaria Vaccines
what: The first malaria vaccines recommended for children in endemic regions, now in national immunisation rollouts across parts of Africa.
how: Pre-erythrocytic subunit vaccines targeting the parasite before it reaches the bloodstream.

name: Neglected Tropical Disease Elimination
use: Diseases affecting over a billion people
what: Mass drug administration and vector-control programmes targeting diseases such as lymphatic filariasis, trachoma and river blindness, several now eliminated in individual countries.
how: Population-wide preventive chemotherapy plus vector control and surveillance.

name: Shorter TB Drug Regimens
what: All-oral treatment courses that cut drug-resistant TB therapy from around two years to six months, replacing painful injectable regimens.
how: Combination regimens built on newer agents such as bedaquiline and pretomanid.

name: In-Vivo Base Editing
what: One-time gene-editing therapies delivered directly into the body to correct or switch off a disease-causing gene without cutting both DNA strands.
how: Lipid nanoparticles carry a base-editor and guide RNA to the liver, where a single DNA letter is chemically converted, changing the gene's output.
use: Inherited cardiovascular and metabolic disease (clinical trials)

name: Next-Generation TB Vaccines
what: Candidate vaccines aiming to protect adults against tuberculosis, which the century-old BCG vaccine does poorly. TB remains one of the largest infectious killers worldwide.
how: Subunit and viral-vector candidates in late-stage efficacy trials.

name: AI-Driven Drug Discovery
what: AI models predict drug efficacy and side effects for individual patients.
how: Machine learning algorithms analyze vast datasets to identify potential treatments.

name: CAR-T 2.0
use: Next-generation CAR-T therapies targeting a broader range of cancers
what: Improves the efficacy and safety of CAR-T therapies by targeting a broader range of cancers with higher specificity.
how: This technology could significantly improve outcomes for patients with refractory cancers.

name: CRISPR Gene Editing for Therapy
what: Precisely modifies DNA sequences in cells.
how: Uses CRISPR-Cas9 technology to target and edit specific genes.

name: Longevity Medicine
what: Longevity medicine focuses on extending human lifespan through a combination of regenerative therapies, gene editing, and lifestyle interventions. Breakthroughs in this field could significantly reduce age-related diseases.
how: This involves using CRISPR technology to edit genes associated with aging and developing new drugs for age-related conditions.

name: Precision Fermentation for Biomanufacturing
what: Precision fermentation uses engineered microorganisms to produce complex molecules at scale.
how: This technology allows for the efficient and cost-effective production of biologics like monoclonal antibodies and viral vectors.

name: Precision Oncology
what: Use of CRISPR for targeted gene editing to enhance cancer treatments and improve patient outcomes.
how: These treatments offer better outcomes and fewer side effects than traditional methods.

name: Thermostable Vaccines
what: Vaccine formulations that survive without refrigeration, removing the cold-chain requirement that blocks delivery to remote regions.
how: Lyophilised and glass-matrix formulations that stabilise antigens at ambient temperature.

name: Cellular Reprogramming
what: The process of resetting adult somatic cells to a pluripotent or more youthful state.
how: Utilizes partial expression of Yamanaka factors (OSKM) to reverse epigenetic aging markers without inducing pluripotency.

name: Genetic Engineering for Aging
use: Developing genetic therapies to extend human lifespan and improve healthspan.
what: Using CRISPR and other gene editing tools to target age-related diseases and cellular senescence.
how: Identifying key genes involved in aging processes and developing targeted interventions.

name: Longevity Biotechnology (Altos Labs)
what: Research and development focused on extending human lifespan through biotechnological interventions.
how: Involves stem cell therapy, gene editing, and tissue regeneration technologies.

name: mRNA Therapeutics
use: Advanced drug development and personalized medicine
what: mRNA therapeutics use messenger RNA to instruct cells to produce therapeutic proteins, offering potential treatments for a wide range of diseases including genetic disorders and cancer.
how: Developing microfluidic devices that mimic human organs, next-generation CAR-T therapies, and using mRNA to deliver targeted gene therapy.

name: Organ-on-Chip
what: Organ-on-chip technology involves creating miniature, functional human organs for research and drug testing. This could revolutionize medical research by providing more accurate models of human physiology.
how: This involves developing microfluidic devices that mimic the structure and function of real organs.

name: Regenerative Medicine
what: A field that focuses on repairing or replacing damaged tissues and organs using stem cells.
how: Utilizes pluripotent stem cell technology for tissue regeneration.

name: Synthetic Organs
what: Future medical technologies are developing methods for biofabricating entire organs from stem cells and other biological materials to replace damaged tissues.
how: Replicates the structure and function of human tissues using bioinks and living cells.

name: Advanced AI Agents in Medicine
what: AI agents can analyze vast amounts of medical data to provide personalized treatment plans.
how: These agents use machine learning to predict patient outcomes and suggest optimal treatments.

name: Advanced Prosthetics
what: Customized prosthetic limbs with integrated sensors and AI for enhanced mobility.
how: AI algorithms analyze patient data to optimize fit and function.

name: Biodegradable Nanoparticles for Drug Delivery
what: Nanoparticles designed to degrade naturally within the body, improving drug delivery.
how: Enhanced efficacy and safety of treatments.

name: Digital Afterlife
what: Digital afterlife technologies will allow for the preservation and continuation of consciousness post-mortem.
how: Using advanced AI to simulate and maintain a digital version of the individual’s mind.

name: Gene Editing for Neurodegenerative Diseases
use: Targeting genetic mutations in neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's
what: Advanced gene editing techniques like base and prime editing.
how: Potential to develop targeted therapies.
companies: Editas Medicine · CRISPR Therapeutics · Sangamo Biosciences

name: Gene Editing for Organ Regeneration
what: Advanced gene editing techniques to regenerate damaged organs.
how: CRISPR-Cas9 and prime editing technology.

name: Gene Editing with CRISPR 3.0
what: Includes base editing and prime editing for more precise gene modifications.
how: Reduces off-target effects, enabling safer and more effective treatments.
companies: Editas Medicine · CRISPR Therapeutics · Intellia Therapeutics

name: Mind Uploading
what: Mind uploading involves transferring a person's consciousness into a digital format for long-term storage or transfer.
how: By mapping the neural connections and patterns of an individual's brain, their mind can be uploaded to a computer.

name: Nanotechnology in Medicine
what: Nanoparticles for targeted drug delivery and non-invasive diagnostic tools.
how: Nanomaterials enhance the precision of medical interventions.

name: Neural Engineering Interfaces (NEI)
what: Directly interfaces with the human nervous system.
how: Enables advanced control and treatment of neurological disorders.
companies: Bryan Johnson's Kernel · DARPA · MIT Media Lab

name: Neural Prosthetics
use: Restoration of motor functions, cognitive enhancement
what: Advanced neural prosthetics enable direct brain-computer interaction for restoring lost functions and enhancing human capabilities.
how: By integrating with the brain's natural neural networks, these interfaces can restore or augment sensory and motor functions.

name: Synthetic Biology Applications in Medicine
what: CRISPR 3.0 for precise gene editing and targeted drug delivery.
how: Advanced CRISPR tools enable more efficient and accurate genetic modifications.

name: Synthetic Ecosystems for Carbon Capture
use: Capture and process carbon dioxide more efficiently than natural systems.
what: Designs synthetic ecosystems to sequester CO2 directly from the atmosphere.
how: Utilizes biotechnology to enhance carbon capture efficiency.

name: Synthetic Organoids
what: Three-dimensional, miniaturized versions of human organs used for drug testing and personalized medicine.
how: Enabling more accurate and efficient drug testing and personalized medicine through organ-on-a-chip technology.

name: AI Chest X-Ray Screening
use: TB triage where radiologists are scarce
what: Software that reads chest X-rays for tuberculosis signs, WHO-recommended as a triage tool in settings with few radiologists.
how: Deep-learning classifiers on portable digital X-ray systems.

name: Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance
use: Tracking the rise of untreatable infection
what: Genomic and clinical surveillance networks tracking resistant pathogens. Drug-resistant infection is among the leading causes of death associated with infectious disease worldwide.
how: Whole-genome sequencing of isolates linked to shared international databases.

name: Liquid Biopsy
what: Liquid biopsies involve analyzing circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in blood samples to detect cancer. This technology allows for earlier detection, monitoring of treatment response, and personalized therapy selection.
how: Ultra-sensitive sequencing and methylation analysis of cell-free DNA flag tumour signals and tissue of origin from a routine blood draw.

name: Point-of-Care Molecular Diagnostics
what: Battery-capable molecular tests that identify pathogens and drug resistance in under an hour at clinic level, rather than days via a reference laboratory.
how: Cartridge-based PCR and isothermal amplification platforms.

name: Brain Organoid Disease Models
what: Miniature 3D brain tissues grown from stem cells to study disease and test drugs on human neurons.
how: Pluripotent stem cells self-organise into layered neural tissue in culture, reproducing aspects of cortical development.

name: Organ-on-Chip: Artificial Organs for Drug Testing
use: Accurate and Efficient Testing, Reducing Animal Testing
what: Creating microscale models of human organs to test drugs and study diseases.
how: Through advanced microfluidic technology and tissue engineering.

name: Sickle-Cell Gene Therapy
what: Approved gene therapies that functionally cure sickle-cell disease — among the first CRISPR-based medicines authorised anywhere. Cost and cold-chain logistics limit reach in the countries with the highest burden.
how: Patient stem cells edited to restore fetal haemoglobin, then re-infused.

name: Base Editing
what: Precise single-letter DNA edits delivered directly inside the body, avoiding the double-strand breaks of first-generation CRISPR.
how: A base or prime editor is packaged in lipid nanoparticles or viral vectors and delivered to target tissue, chemically converting one base to another.
use: Genetic liver, eye and blood disorders

name: Cancer Genomics
what: Advanced sequencing and analysis of cancer genomes.
how: Tailored therapies based on genetic profiles.

name: CRISPR Gene Editing for Genetic Disorders
what: CRISPR technology is advancing rapidly, offering precise gene editing capabilities to treat genetic disorders at the molecular level.
how: Development of CRISPR-based therapies and delivery systems.

name: Epigenetic Reprogramming
what: Resetting cellular identity to a younger state without losing cell specialization.
how: Transient expression of Yamanaka factors (OSKM) to reverse the epigenetic clock.

name: In-Vivo CRISPR Therapies
what: Gene-editing therapies delivered directly into the body to correct disease-causing mutations, moving beyond ex-vivo cell editing.
how: Lipid nanoparticles or viral vectors carry CRISPR machinery to target tissues such as the liver, where it edits the faulty gene in place.

name: Gene-Drive Mosquitoes
what: Mosquitoes engineered so an inherited trait spreads through wild populations to crash them or block parasite transmission. Powerful, and irreversible enough that governance is an open question.
how: CRISPR-based drives biased to inherit far more often than the usual half.

name: Gene Editing for Genetic Diseases
what: Advanced gene editing technologies like CRISPR-Cas9 are poised to revolutionize the treatment of genetic diseases, offering potential cures.
how: Tailored genome modifications for targeted therapeutic interventions.

name: CRISPR 4.0
what: Advanced base editing and prime editing capabilities for precise genome modifications.
how: Edit genes without double-strand breaks.

name: CRISPR Gene Drives
what: Spreads beneficial genetic traits through populations of organisms.
how: Used to solve issues like malaria and invasive species control.

name: Gene-Editing Beyond CRISPR
use: Treating genetic disorders, enhancing gene functions
what: Offers precise modifications to DNA without double-strand breaks.
how: Base editing and prime editing technologies.

name: Genome Editing for Organ Regeneration
use: Curing Diseases Like Diabetes, Kidney Failure
what: Advanced genome editing techniques enable organ regeneration.
how: Replaces damaged tissues with healthy ones to cure diseases.

name: Precision OncoLogic
what: Integrates advanced AI and genomics for tailored treatment plans.
how: Analyzes patient data to identify genetic markers and optimize treatments.

name: AI Radiology Triage
what: Clinically-validated models that flag urgent findings on scans and act as a second reader, cutting time-to-diagnosis for strokes and cancers.
how: Deep networks trained on labelled imaging datasets score studies for critical findings and route them up the radiologist worklist.

name: Gene-Edited Xenotransplantation
what: Transplanting organs from gene-edited pigs into humans to address the chronic shortage of donor organs.
how: Donor pigs have multiple genes edited to remove pig-specific antigens and retroviruses and add human compatibility genes; organs are placed under close monitoring.
use: Kidney and heart transplantation (early clinical cases)

name: Low-Cost Maternal Health Diagnostics
what: Portable ultrasound and low-cost screening tools for pre-eclampsia and postpartum haemorrhage risk, aimed at the settings where maternal deaths are concentrated.
how: Handheld probes with AI guidance for non-specialist operators.

name: Lab-Grown Transplant Organs
what: Functional human organs grown from cells for transplant, aiming to remove donor shortages and rejection.
how: Patient cells are seeded onto decellularised scaffolds or 3D-bioprinted, then matured in bioreactors until vascularised and functional.

name: Organ-on-Chip and Personalised Medicine
what: Organ-on-chip technology is advancing personalized medicine by creating miniature human organs for testing drugs and studying diseases.
how: Miniature organs can simulate complex biological processes.

name: Organ-on-Chip Technology for Drug Testing
what: Simulates human organs in microfluidic devices.
how: Predict drug performance and side effects in vitro.

name: Quantum Medical Devices
what: Developing quantum devices that can diagnose and treat diseases at a molecular level.
how: Using quantum sensors to detect and target specific biological markers.

name: Senolytic Therapeutics
what: Drugs designed to selectively induce apoptosis in senescent 'zombie' cells.
how: Targeting the BCL-2 family of proteins to bypass the pro-survival pathways of old cells.

name: Prime Editing
what: A 'search-and-replace' genome editing technology that does not require double-strand breaks.
how: Fusing a catalytically impaired Cas9 to a reverse transcriptase, using a pegRNA to rewrite DNA.

name: Senolytic Therapy
what: Drugs designed to selectively induce apoptosis in senescent cells.
how: Targets anti-apoptotic pathways (like Bcl-2) specifically in non-dividing, pro-inflammatory cells.

name: Senolytics
what: Small molecules designed to selectively induce death in senescent 'zombie' cells.
how: Targets anti-apoptotic pathways that allow damaged cells to survive.

name: Multi-Cancer Early Detection (MCED)
what: Blood tests that detect fragmented DNA (cfDNA) and methylation patterns.
how: High-throughput sequencing of plasma to identify cancer signals.

name: Biological Age Reversal
what: Treatments that restore systemic cellular youth and organ function.
how: Epigenetic reprogramming via OSKM factors and senolytic clearance.

name: Molecular Nanobot Surgeons
what: Autonomous nanomachines that repair DNA damage and remove pathogens at the molecular level.
how: Programmed with molecular recognition logic to target specific protein signatures.

name: Biologic Backup Storage
what: The ability to encode massive digital datasets into synthetic non-coding DNA within living cells.
how: Uses CRISPR-based writing to insert digitally encoded data into the genome of a dormant cell line.
